rules.fix: USE THE MACRO — call your field macro (button/select/input/textarea); the fleet has one for each (buttons.html, forms.html). The `<form>` wrapper itself stays raw (page-specific action/method) — compose raw `<form>` + field macros, the fleet standard. Fixing this red means finding and calling the field macro, not exempting: even a showcase page renders its macros. Scans ALL templates (pages, partials, flat) except macros/ — a raw component is wrong wherever it composes. [templates].exempt is a LAST resort for a single deliberate raw-vs-macro comparison line (with evidence). A single DELIBERATE counter-example (e.g. a component showcase demonstrating the wrong pattern next to the macro) may carry an inline `{# no_hand_rolled_components_in_pages: <reason> #}` waiver on, or in the comment block directly above, the line — reason REQUIRED. That is the per-LINE carve-out; do NOT stand the rule down on the whole page with [templates].exempt.

rules.inert_reason: this app renders a page by a computed name (a non-literal TemplateResponse), so an unreferenced page can't be proven dead. Orphan detection runs only when every render uses a literal template name.

rules.fix: Move the Enum class to app/models/enum_model.py (or enums.py), or to its domain submodule of the package app/models/enum_model/ (import from the submodule, no re-export), and import it where used — enums cross every layer by design (ADR-001) so they have one home, and a stray enum is caught only by ricochet off another rule (or not at all, if only a core/service imports it). If it's genuinely NOT a model enum (error-infrastructure core owns, not DB-persisted, and moving it makes an import cycle), exempt it: [allowlist].enum_placement = [{ enum, evidence }]. See --playbook enum-typing.

Add each enum to `[enums].declared` in .luxarch.toml. Placement (enums_in_enum_model) gives it one home; declaration is what makes the value/column rules examine it — without it the enum is invisible to enforcement, so a move without a declaration only relocates the problem. Declaring a column-less enum is harmless (those rules stay inert for it). See --playbook enum-typing.

rules.fix: Move the DTO to `app/schemas/<domain>_schema.py` and import it where it's built. A DTO defined inside a service is invisible to the schema-scanning rules — most importantly fw.enum_dto_fields_enum_typed — so its closed-set fields go unchecked and the enum family reads green over untyped data. Relocation is mechanical: the type moves, the boundary stays typed. Do this BEFORE fw.no_inline_imports — a lazy import usually exists to dodge the circular dependency a misplaced DTO created, and lifts on its own once the DTO moves. Internal value types never returned outward are not flagged. See --playbook burn-down-order §2.

rules.inert_reason: the harness isolates by holding ONE connection and rolling it back (apps/backend/tests/fixtures/db.py:109), so a pooled test engine cannot work here — each pytest-asyncio test gets its own loop and a pooled connection belongs to the loop that opened it. **This INERT is the correct END STATE for such a harness, not a todo.** Do NOT migrate to DELETE/TRUNCATE-per-test to satisfy this rule: luxlint's test.no_handrolled_cleanup exists to red exactly that, and rollback isolation is the better pattern (faster, no table-ordering bugs, nothing to forget). An earlier version of this message named that migration as the prerequisite and was wrong — it pointed at something another fleet guard forbids. Measured, pursuing pooling here costs you: 0 failures on NullPool, 139 pooled, 366 pooled+dispose. And you lose nothing in DETECTION — the cross-session visibility class this rule guards is caught by durability locks that read on a SEPARATE connection, which works whatever the pool class. Pool the APP engine (fw.dev_prod_pool_parity); leave the test engine alone.

rules.fix: bound every image to a version line: `nginx:1.31-alpine`, not `nginx:alpine` or `:latest`. Where the fleet keeps a line (`luxarch --fleet-versions`), use that line; patches float under it, which is the point, and a move to the next line is a deliberate fleet bump the owner makes in ONE home. No digests, no exact freezes. A data-bearing image (postgres and its extension images) is judged only for being unbounded: its major is a dump-and-restore. See --doc FLEET-BUILD-DEPLOY-STANDARD, 'Image lines'.
